text: If you face unfair treatment, illegal fees, or rejected transactions by a financial institution, you should follow the official three-step Path to Justice: first, lodge a formal complaint directly with the specific Financial Service Provider (FSP) at the branch or customer care level.

As the second step in resolving a banking dispute, if your complaint is not resolved satisfactorily at the branch level, you must escalate the matter to the Financial Service Provider's head-office complaints unit.

As the final step in the Path to Justice, if all internal complaint options with your financial service provider are exhausted without resolution, you can contact the Bank of Zambia to independently review your case.

The Bank of Zambia provides official communication channels including telephone, email, and in-person visits at its Head Office and regional offices for consumers to submit formal escalated complaints.

text: The Bank of Zambia collaborates with industry bodies such as the GSMA of Zambia and law enforcement agencies to run nationwide fraud awareness campaigns against mobile-related financial fraud and cybercrime.

Consumers are strongly advised to remain vigilant in protecting both their finances and confidential personal information against sophisticated cybercrime syndicates operating across digital and mobile platforms.

The Zambia Police Service and the Bank of Zambia have issued joint warnings regarding the growing threat of cybercrime and payment fraud, urging citizens to secure their credentials and report suspicious activities.
The Bank of Zambia's market-conduct supervision ensures that Financial Service Providers operate fairly, transparently, and adhere to strict consumer protection standards across all banking products.
A safe financial product, as defined under Bank of Zambia consumer protection standards, is one that is secure, fully transparent in pricing and terms, and fair to everyday consumers.

Under the National Financial Inclusion Strategy, the Bank of Zambia prioritizes strengthening consumer protection frameworks and increasing financial capabilities to protect consumers against emerging market risks.
Cheques were officially phased out as a payment instrument in Zambia on 24 June 2026, marking a decisive transition toward a fully digital 24/7 financial economy.
source_title: Zambanker - March 2025 (Special Edition on Cheques & Currency)

text: Electronic Funds Transfers (EFTs) are processed in batches through the Direct Debit and Credit Clearing (DDACC) system for routine commercial transfers, salaries, and bill payments.
source_title: Zambanker - March 2025 (Special Edition on Cheques & Currency)

text: Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) is designed by the Bank of Zambia for high-value and time-critical payments, supporting transaction values starting from 1 ngwee up to very large corporate transfers.
source_title: Zambanker - March 2025 (Special Edition on Cheques & Currency)

text: Mobile money remains the primary driver of financial inclusion in Zambia, enabling interoperable digital transactions across different platforms and institutions via the national payment infrastructure.
The Bank of Zambia regulates commercial banks and authorized financial service institutions registered under the Banking and Financial Services Act to maintain financial stability.
Consumers can verify whether a financial institution or commercial bank is officially authorized by checking the official Bank of Zambia registered institutions directory on the official website.
The Bank of Zambia, in partnership with the Ministry of Finance and National Planning and the Bankers Association of Zambia, promotes continuous year-round financial literacy to educate the public.
The Bank of Zambia released an official educational mobile application alongside the K100 and K50 banknotes to help members of the public easily identify currency security features.
source_title: Public Notice: Launch of the K100 and K50 Banknotes and Release of an Educational App on the New Currency

text: According to the FinScope 2025 Survey published by the Bank of Zambia, overall financial inclusion in Zambia rose to 80.1 percent, driven largely by the expansion of mobile money services.
Applicants intending to conduct payment system business must submit formal applications to the Bank of Zambia detailing their business structure, policies, and risk management frameworks.
source_title: Requirements for Designating a Payment System

text: Payment system applicants must satisfy the Bank of Zambia that they maintain robust Anti-Money Laundering (AML/CFT) and Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures to prevent financial crimes.
source_title: Requirements for Designating a Payment System

text: The Bank of Zambia determines an application for designation of a payment system within a period of ninety days from the date of receipt of a duly completed application.
source_title: Requirements for Designating a Payment System

The Bank of Zambia Regional Office is located at Buteko Avenue, P.O. Box 71511, Ndola, Zambia, with official telephone contact (+260) 212 399 600.
The Bank of Zambia's strategic plan prioritizes cyber security resilience, market-conduct supervision, and improved dispute resolution to protect financial consumers across Zambia.

When encountering suspected financial scams or fraud, consumers should refrain from sharing sensitive banking credentials and immediately report the incident to their financial provider and law enforcement.
